name: Titius Justus
title: God-fearing host in Corinth
summary: Titius Justus was a God-fearing man in Corinth who opened his home to the apostle Paul after he left the synagogue. His house was located right next to the synagogue and became an important gathering place for the early Christian community in Corinth. He is known as one who feared God, indicating that he was a Gentile who sympathized with Judaism before becoming a Christian.

keyEvents.title: Paul leaves the synagogue in Corinth
keyEvents.description: When the Jews in Corinth opposed Paul's preaching, he left the synagogue and went to the house of Titius Justus, a God-fearing man who lived right next to the synagogue.

keyEvents.title: Titius Justus opens his home
keyEvents.description: Titius Justus welcomed Paul and allowed his home to be used as a meeting place for believers in Corinth, demonstrating his hospitality and devotion to the gospel.

keyEvents.title: Crispus and many Corinthians come to faith
keyEvents.description: While Paul was staying in the house of Titius Justus, the synagogue ruler Crispus came to believe along with his entire household, and many other Corinthians became believers and were baptized.

keyEvents.title: The Lord's encouragement to Paul in Corinth
keyEvents.description: While Paul was working from the home of Titius Justus, the Lord spoke to him in a night vision and encouraged him to continue preaching in Corinth without fear, for God had many people in the city.
